# CoachLab code walkthrough

Source walkthrough updated for production deployment preparation on 2026-10-27 (on top of the login, lesson manager and media work). Local development explicitly uses Neon PostgreSQL; SQLite remains the default alternative. Exact listing coverage is checked against files; real-browser results are reported in AUTH_SECURITY_REPORT.md.

Every line, including blank lines and closing delimiters, is listed below. Numbered code blocks are for reading; remove line-number prefixes before copying code. Paths are exact repository-relative paths, with the current absolute workspace path given for each file.

## How the pieces connect

Browser: Vite serves index.html, main.jsx mounts App, and App fetches the lesson list through Vite's /api proxy. Express validates requests and awaits the selected lesson store. Local development explicitly selects the guarded Prisma client and Neon Development; an unset selector uses external SQLite. There is no automatic fallback. The browser never sees database credentials.

Manual creation and saved editing share LessonForm. An existing lesson selects PUT /api/lessons/:id; a new lesson selects POST /api/lessons. Both send only seven editable fields. ID and creation time remain database-owned. LessonCard offers delete confirmation before DELETE /api/lessons/:id. App updates its local list only after confirmed responses. Refresh reloads persisted rows from the database.

AI generation sends generic class parameters to POST /api/ai/lesson-draft. The Express limiter/validator calls the server-only Gemini provider; response validation checks every guidance field and the five-section duration total. The unsaved draft stays in React state. ActivityEditor supports ordered text cards in either form. Editing resets AI approval. Explicit approval maps guidance to existing goal/drills/coaching_notes fields, then uses the normal POST route. Provider outages do not disable manual CRUD.

LessonCard turns saved text into headings, cues and expandable details without rewriting records. LessonMedia matches a fixed source-reviewed catalog locally and loads publisher media only on disclosure/playback actions. Missing matches, images or embeds retain explanatory text/source links. No automatic media search or model-generated URL is trusted.

Media: every activity card in LessonForm (and every section of an AI draft) shows an Add Media button. MediaEditor lets a coach upload a picture or video (POST /api/media/upload; the server checks the real file bytes and stores them in the lesson_media table) or paste a link (POST /api/media/verify; the server fetches the link safely and confirms it is a real picture, video or YouTube video). Nothing is attached to a lesson until Save: the form sends the list in the lesson's POST or PUT body, the server verifies any new links again, and the store attaches everything in the same database transaction as the lesson. Attachments find their activity through its heading line, so they follow it when it is renamed. After an AI draft is generated, the browser calls POST /api/media/suggest; media-finder.js combines the reviewed catalog, Wikimedia Commons and (if a server-side key exists) YouTube search, verifies every address and returns only verified items for the section that asked. App loads GET /api/lesson-media and gives each LessonCard its own attachments. Uploaded files are served by GET /api/media/:id/file with byte-range support. client/api-proxy.js forwards /api from the Vite development server because Vite's built-in proxy stalls on files over about 1 MB.

Accounts: main.jsx now mounts Gate, which asks GET /api/auth/get-session whether the browser has a valid session and shows either AuthScreen (sign in, create account, forgot password, choose new password) or the dashboard App. The login routes under /api/auth are served by the Better Auth library (server/auth.js): passwords are hashed with scrypt, sessions live in the database and are carried by an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie, sign-in is rate limited per address and per account, and password reset links are single-use and expire after an hour (until an email provider exists they are printed in the backend window by mailer.js). Every other /api route passes through one gate in app.js that requires a valid session and, for changes, an allowed Origin; the signed-in coach's id is passed to the stores, which filter every query by owner_id, so another coach's lessons and media answer 404. Lessons created before accounts have no owner and are invisible to everyone until the operator runs npm run claim-lessons (claim.js), which defaults to a dry run, writes a verified backup, and only touches unowned lessons.

Prisma generation emits ignored TypeScript and compiled ESM. Development startup does not run PostgreSQL migrations. The separately approved production npm start now validates settings and runs Prisma migrate deploy before serving Express; see DEPLOY.md. Existing table constraints remain in effect. Isolated PostgreSQL tests use explicit random schemas; ordinary npm test uses disposable SQLite plus pure browser-data helpers.

## Reading the syntax

JavaScript executes application logic. JSX is HTML-like syntax inside JavaScript that Vite converts into React calls. A component is a function that returns UI; state remembers values between renders; an effect synchronizes with something outside rendering, such as a network request. Props are inputs passed to components: App passes lesson data to LessonCard and callback functions to LessonForm. HTML attributes configure elements. JSON is a data format, not executable JavaScript. CSS controls appearance. Parentheses group expressions or pass function arguments; braces can delimit code blocks, objects, imports, or JSX expressions depending on context.


- **Line 1:** Human-readable comment: Loads the React entry point; the app fills the root element after login checks. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 2:** Declares modern HTML so the browser uses standard page rendering.
- **Line 3:** Opens the page element; lang="en" identifies English for accessibility tools.
- **Line 4:** Opens head, the section containing page metadata rather than visible content.
- **Line 5:** Sets UTF-8 text encoding, allowing characters such as the ellipsis. This metadata element has no closing tag.
- **Line 6:** Makes the viewport match the device width and starts at normal zoom, supporting mobile layout.
- **Line 7:** Sets the browser tab title to CoachLab; the closing title tag ends that text.
- **Line 8:** Closes the head metadata section.
- **Line 9:** Opens the body, which contains the visible page.
- **Line 10:** Creates and immediately closes an empty div with ID root. React fills this container later.
- **Line 11:** Loads /src/main.jsx as a JavaScript module; Vite transforms its JSX for the browser. The closing script tag ends this element.
- **Line 12:** Closes the body.
- **Line 13:** Closes the entire HTML document.

- **Line 121:** Opens the page header and applies the hero CSS class using JSX's className attribute.

Selects a local SQLite path outside OneDrive to avoid cloud-sync database conflicts.

### Lines 1–16

```text
1 | // Selects a local SQLite path outside OneDrive to avoid cloud-sync database conflicts.
2 | import { homedir } from 'node:os';
3 | import path from 'node:path';
4 |
5 | // This only chooses the future database location; it does not create a database.
6 | export const databasePath = process.env.DATABASE_PATH?.trim()
7 |   || path.join(homedir(), 'AppData', 'Local', 'CoachLab', 'coachlab.sqlite');
8 |
9 | if (!path.isAbsolute(databasePath)) {
10 |   throw new Error('DATABASE_PATH must be an absolute path outside OneDrive.');
11 | }
12 |
13 | // Cloud sync can race database writes; require the SQLite file outside OneDrive.
14 | if (path.resolve(databasePath).split(path.sep).some(part => /^onedrive(?:\s|$)/i.test(part))) {
15 |   throw new Error('DATABASE_PATH must be outside OneDrive.');
16 | }
```

- **Line 1:** Human-readable comment: Selects a local SQLite path outside OneDrive to avoid cloud-sync database conflicts. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 2:** Imports the named homedir function from Node's built-in operating-system module; node: explicitly identifies a built-in module.
- **Line 3:** Imports Node's path utilities as a default import for platform-aware path operations.
- **Line 4:** Blank line separates related sections for readability; it performs no operation.
- **Line 5:** Human-readable comment: This only chooses the future database location; it does not create a database. Comments explain intent and are not executed.
- **Line 6:** Exports a constant databasePath. process.env reads backend environment variables; ?. calls trim only when DATABASE_PATH exists. trim removes surrounding whitespace. The expression continues on the next line.
- **Line 7:** The || operator selects the fallback when the configured value is absent or empty. path.join combines the user's home directory and these folder/file names using Windows separators here; the semicolon ends the assignment.
- **Line 8:** Blank line separates related sections for readability; it performs no operation.
- **Line 9:** Checks whether the selected path is not absolute. ! reverses the Boolean result of isAbsolute; braces open the conditional block.
- **Line 10:** Throws an Error with an actionable message. A thrown error during import prevents normal server startup.
- **Line 11:** Closes the absolute-path validation block.
- **Line 12:** Blank line separates related sections for readability; it performs no operation.
- **Line 13:** Human-readable comment: Cloud sync can race database writes; require the SQLite file outside OneDrive. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 14:** Resolves and normalizes the path, splits it into folder parts using path.sep, and uses some to check whether any part matches. part =&gt; is an arrow predicate. The regex starts at the beginning (^), matches onedrive followed by whitespace (\s) or end ($), groups alternatives with (?:...|...), and ignores case with i. It is a folder-name heuristic, not detection of arbitrary sync roots or filesystem links.
- **Line 15:** Rejects a matching OneDrive folder with an Error before the server starts.
- **Line 16:** Closes the absolute-path validation block.

## server/migrations/001_create_lessons.sql

Exact path: `C:\Users\barri\OneDrive\Desktop\Next Chapter Projects\CoachLab\server\migrations\001_create_lessons.sql`

Version 1 of the schema. migrations.js reads this fixed local SQL file and executes it within a transaction. SQL keywords describe database operations; commas separate columns and constraints. Do not edit a migration already applied to shared databases: add a new version instead.

### Lines 1–11

```text
1 | CREATE TABLE lessons (
2 |   id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
3 |   title TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(title)) > 0),
4 |   discipline TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (discipline IN ('Boxing', 'Wrestling', 'Muay Thai', 'Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu', 'MMA', 'Personal Training')),
5 |   skill_level TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Beginner' CHECK (skill_level IN ('Beginner', 'Intermediate', 'Advanced')),
6 |   duration_minutes INTEGER CHECK (duration_minutes > 0),
7 |   goal TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
8 |   drills TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
9 |   coaching_notes TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
10 |   created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
11 | ) STRICT;
```

- **Line 1:** CREATE TABLE defines a new lessons table; the opening parenthesis begins its column definitions. The runner checks its version before executing this statement.
- **Line 2:** Defines id as the integer primary key, a unique row identifier. In SQLite this aliases the row ID and is generated when an insert omits it. A comma separates the next column.
- **Line 3:** Requires a text title that is not NULL. CHECK evaluates length(trim(title)) &gt; 0: remove ordinary surrounding spaces, count remaining characters, and reject zero length. This does not replace future API validation for all whitespace or length rules.
- **Line 4:** Requires a text discipline chosen from the six quoted values. IN tests membership; the parentheses hold the choices and close the CHECK expression.
- **Line 5:** Requires skill_level text, defaults it to Beginner when omitted, and restricts it to the three listed values with CHECK and IN.
- **Line 6:** Defines duration_minutes as an integer. CHECK rejects zero or negative values. With no NOT NULL constraint, NULL is allowed to represent an unspecified duration; STRICT rejects fractional values that cannot become integers.
- **Line 7:** Requires goal text and supplies the empty string default when omitted; two single quotes mean an empty SQL string.
- **Line 8:** Requires drills text with an empty-string default.
- **Line 9:** Requires coaching_notes text with an empty-string default.
- **Line 10:** Requires a creation timestamp as text. DEFAULT evaluates strftime using SQLite's current UTC time; %Y/%m/%d are date pieces, %H/%M/%f are hours/minutes/seconds with fractions, T separates date/time, and Z indicates UTC. Parentheses enclose the default expression.
- **Line 11:** Closes the table definition and enables STRICT typing, so stored values must conform to the column types under SQLite's conversion rules. The semicolon ends the SQL statement.

## server/migrations.js

Exact path: `C:\Users\barri\OneDrive\Desktop\Next Chapter Projects\CoachLab\server\migrations.js`

Records SQLite migration versions so each reviewed SQL file is applied only once.

### Lines 1–20

```text
1 | // Records SQLite migration versions so each reviewed SQL file is applied only once.
2 | import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
3 |
4 | // Applies each SQLite SQL version inside a transaction and records it only on success.
5 | export function migrate(database) {
6 |   database.exec(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (
7 |     version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
8 |     applied_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
9 |   ) STRICT`);
10 |   const migrations = [{ version: 1, file: '001_create_lessons.sql' }, { version: 2, file: '002_create_lesson_media.sql' }, { version: 3, file: '003_add_ownership.sql' }, { version: 4, file: '004_add_lesson_audience.sql' }];
11 |   for (const migration of migrations) {
12 |     database.transaction(() => {
13 |       const applied = database.prepare('SELECT version FROM schema_migrations WHERE version = ?').get(migration.version);
14 |       if (applied) return;
15 |       const sql = readFileSync(new URL(`./migrations/${migration.file}`, import.meta.url), 'utf8');
16 |       database.exec(sql);
17 |       database.prepare('INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES (?)').run(migration.version);
18 |     })();
19 |   }
20 | }
```

- **Line 1:** Human-readable comment: Records SQLite migration versions so each reviewed SQL file is applied only once. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 2:** Imports the named readFileSync function to read migration SQL from disk as text.
- **Line 3:** Blank line separates related sections for readability; it performs no operation.
- **Line 4:** Human-readable comment: Applies each SQLite SQL version inside a transaction and records it only on success. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 5:** Exports migrate, a function taking an already-open database connection; braces open its body.
- **Line 6:** Begins a multiline template string containing SQL and passes it to exec. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS creates the tracking table only when it is missing; parentheses open its columns. Backticks delimit multiline JavaScript strings.
- **Line 7:** Defines the tracking version as a unique integer primary key. The comma separates the timestamp column.
- **Line 8:** Defines a required applied_at UTC timestamp with a default evaluated at insertion, using the same strftime format as lesson timestamps.
- **Line 9:** Closes the tracking table columns, enables STRICT typing, closes the template string and exec call, and ends the JavaScript statement. Creating this bookkeeping table occurs before each version transaction.
- **Line 10:** Adds SQLite migration version four to the ordered list. The version table prevents rerunning its ALTER TABLE statement.
- **Line 11:** Iterates the descriptors with for...of. const migration holds the current descriptor; braces open the loop.
- **Line 12:** Creates a transaction wrapper around the arrow callback. The callback's queries will run as one atomic unit when the wrapper is called below.
- **Line 13:** Prepares a SELECT query with a ? placeholder and binds the current version through get. This keeps data separate from SQL syntax; get returns one row or undefined.
- **Line 14:** If a version row already exists, returns from this transaction callback without changing lessons. The outer loop can still continue to later migrations.
- **Line 15:** Builds a file URL relative to this module using import.meta.url and interpolates the fixed migration filename using a dollar sign followed by braces. readFileSync reads UTF-8 SQL text. No user input supplies this SQL file.
- **Line 16:** Executes the trusted migration SQL, creating the lessons table for version 1. A database failure throws rather than pretending to succeed.
- **Line 17:** Records the version using a parameterized INSERT and run. The applied_at default supplies the timestamp. This insert shares the schema-change transaction.
- **Line 18:** Closes the callback and transaction factory call, then immediately calls the returned wrapper with (). Success commits; an exception rolls back the changes and propagates.
- **Line 19:** Closes migrate.
- **Line 20:** Closes migrate.

```text
9 |   if (target < 0 || target >= next.length) return next;
10 |   [next[index], next[target]] = [next[target], next[index]];

14 | export function activityMinutes(value) {

16 |     const match = block.split('\n')[0].match(/\b(\d{1,3})\s*(?:minutes?|mins?)\b/i);
17 |     return sum + (match ? Number(match[1]) : 0);
18 |   }, 0);
19 | }
```

## server/media-sniff.js

Exact path: `C:\Users\barri\OneDrive\Desktop\Next Chapter Projects\CoachLab\server\media-sniff.js`

Recognizes supported media from file bytes instead of trusting the claimed file type. Checks file signature bytes rather than trusting the filename.

### Lines 1–15

```text
1 | // Recognizes supported media from file bytes instead of trusting the claimed file type.
2 | // Checks file signature bytes rather than trusting the filename.
3 | const startsWith = (buffer, bytes, offset = 0) => bytes.every((byte, index) => buffer[offset + index] === byte);
4 |
5 | // Rejects unknown formats by inspecting the actual bytes.
6 | export function sniffMedia(buffer) {
7 |   if (!buffer || buffer.length < 12) return null;
8 |   if (startsWith(buffer, [0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a])) return { kind: 'image', mime: 'image/png' };
9 |   if (startsWith(buffer, [0xff, 0xd8, 0xff])) return { kind: 'image', mime: 'image/jpeg' };
10 |   if (buffer.subarray(0, 6).toString('latin1') === 'GIF87a' || buffer.subarray(0, 6).toString('latin1') === 'GIF89a') return { kind: 'image', mime: 'image/gif' };
11 |   if (buffer.subarray(0, 4).toString('latin1') === 'RIFF' && buffer.subarray(8, 12).toString('latin1') === 'WEBP') return { kind: 'image', mime: 'image/webp' };
12 |   if (buffer.subarray(4, 8).toString('latin1') === 'ftyp') return { kind: 'video', mime: 'video/mp4' };
13 |   if (startsWith(buffer, [0x1a, 0x45, 0xdf, 0xa3])) return { kind: 'video', mime: 'video/webm' };
14 |   return null;
15 | }
```

- **Line 1:** Human-readable comment: Recognizes supported media from file bytes instead of trusting the claimed file type. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 2:** Human-readable comment: Checks file signature bytes rather than trusting the filename. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 3:** Defines startsWith: true when every expected byte appears in the buffer at the given offset. every() stops at the first mismatch.
- **Line 4:** Blank line separates related sections for readability; it performs no operation.
- **Line 5:** Human-readable comment: Rejects unknown formats by inspecting the actual bytes. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 6:** Exports sniffMedia, which returns the kind (image or video) and exact MIME type of a supported file, or null for anything else.
- **Line 7:** Rejects missing or tiny buffers (under 12 bytes) because they cannot hold a valid signature.
- **Line 8:** PNG files always begin with the eight bytes 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A.
- **Line 9:** JPEG files begin with FF D8 FF.
- **Line 10:** GIF files begin with the text GIF87a or GIF89a; latin1 decoding turns bytes into characters one for one.
- **Line 11:** WebP files are RIFF containers: the text RIFF at the start and WEBP at byte 8.
- **Line 12:** MP4 files carry the text ftyp at byte 4.
- **Line 13:** WebM files begin with the Matroska/EBML marker 1A 45 DF A3.
- **Line 14:** Returns null when no fixed guard reply applies, allowing the model prompt to handle the question.
- **Line 15:** Closes the preceding block (function, object, or statement body).

## server/migrations/002_create_lesson_media.sql

Exact path: `C:\Users\barri\OneDrive\Desktop\Next Chapter Projects\CoachLab\server\migrations\002_create_lesson_media.sql`

Second SQLite migration. It adds a table for pictures and videos attached to lessons; the lessons table is not altered, so existing lessons are untouched.

### Lines 1–18

```text
1 | CREATE TABLE lesson_media (
2 |   id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
3 |   lesson_id INTEGER REFERENCES lessons(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
4 |   position INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
5 |   kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('image', 'video', 'youtube')),
6 |   origin TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (origin IN ('upload', 'link', 'suggested')),
7 |   url TEXT,
8 |   title TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
9 |   activity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
10 |   mime TEXT,
11 |   size_bytes INTEGER,
12 |   data BLOB,
13 |   credit TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
14 |   source_page TEXT,
15 |   created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')),
16 |   CHECK ((origin = 'upload' AND data IS NOT NULL AND url IS NULL) OR (origin <> 'upload' AND data IS NULL AND url IS NOT NULL))
17 | ) STRICT;
18 | CREATE INDEX lesson_media_lesson_id_idx ON lesson_media (lesson_id);
```

- **Line 1:** Creates the lesson_media table.
- **Line 2:** Each attachment gets its own whole-number id.
- **Line 3:** Links to the lesson it belongs to. It may be empty (NULL) while an uploaded file has not been saved with a lesson yet. ON DELETE CASCADE removes attachments when their lesson is deleted.
- **Line 4:** Display order within the lesson, starting at zero.
- **Line 5:** What it is: image, video or youtube. The CHECK refuses any other value.
- **Line 6:** Where it came from: an upload, a link the coach pasted, or a link CoachLab suggested. Other values are refused.
- **Line 7:** The web address for links; empty for uploaded files.
- **Line 8:** Caption shown with the attachment; empty by default.
- **Line 9:** The heading of the activity the attachment belongs to (for example “Warm-up — 10 minutes”); empty means the whole lesson.
- **Line 10:** File type of an uploaded file, such as image/png.
- **Line 11:** Size of an uploaded file in bytes.
- **Line 12:** The uploaded file itself, stored in the database as a BLOB (binary data) so it travels with the database backups and survives restarts.
- **Line 13:** Credit or author text for attribution; empty by default.
- **Line 14:** Link to the page that describes the source or licence.
- **Line 15:** Creation time as an ISO 8601 text timestamp, filled in by SQLite when the row is created. Orphaned uploads are removed by age.
- **Line 16:** Table-level rule: an upload must have file data and no link; a link must have a link and no file data. This keeps rows consistent.
- **Line 17:** Ends the column list. STRICT makes SQLite enforce the declared column types, like the lessons table.
- **Line 18:** Creates an index so finding a lesson’s attachments stays fast.

## prisma/migrations/20261016000100_create_lesson_media/migration.sql

Exact path: `C:\Users\barri\OneDrive\Desktop\Next Chapter Projects\CoachLab\prisma\migrations\20261016000100_create_lesson_media\migration.sql`

PostgreSQL migration that mirrors the SQLite one: it only adds the lesson_media table and an index. It does not change, copy or delete lessons. It has been applied to the Development database only.

### Lines 1–24

```text
1 | BEGIN;
2 | CREATE TABLE "lesson_media" (
3 |   "id" SERIAL NOT NULL,
4 |   "lesson_id" INTEGER,
5 |   "position" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
6 |   "kind" TEXT NOT NULL,
7 |   "origin" TEXT NOT NULL,
8 |   "url" TEXT,
9 |   "title" TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
10 |   "activity" TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
11 |   "mime" TEXT,
12 |   "size_bytes" INTEGER,
13 |   "data" BYTEA,
14 |   "credit" TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
15 |   "source_page" TEXT,
16 |   "created_at" TIMESTAMPTZ(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
17 |   CONSTRAINT "lesson_media_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
18 |   CONSTRAINT "lesson_media_lesson_id_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("lesson_id") REFERENCES "lessons"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
19 |   CONSTRAINT "lesson_media_kind_check" CHECK ("kind" IN ('image', 'video', 'youtube')),
20 |   CONSTRAINT "lesson_media_origin_check" CHECK ("origin" IN ('upload', 'link', 'suggested')),
21 |   CONSTRAINT "lesson_media_source_check" CHECK (("origin" = 'upload' AND "data" IS NOT NULL AND "url" IS NULL) OR ("origin" <> 'upload' AND "data" IS NULL AND "url" IS NOT NULL))
22 | );
23 | CREATE INDEX "lesson_media_lesson_id_idx" ON "lesson_media"("lesson_id");
24 | COMMIT;
```

- **Line 1:** Starts a transaction so the table and index are created together or not at all.
- **Line 2:** Creates the lesson_media table; quoted names keep exact lowercase spelling.
- **Line 3:** SERIAL is an automatically increasing whole-number id.
- **Line 4:** The lesson this attachment belongs to; NULL while an uploaded file is waiting to be saved with a lesson.
- **Line 5:** Display order within the lesson.
- **Line 6:** Attachment kind (image, video or youtube), validated by a CHECK below.
- **Line 7:** Origin (upload, link or suggested), validated by a CHECK below.
- **Line 8:** Web address for linked media; NULL for uploads.
- **Line 9:** Caption, empty by default.
- **Line 10:** Heading of the activity it belongs to; empty means the whole lesson.
- **Line 11:** File type of an upload.
- **Line 12:** File size in bytes.
- **Line 13:** BYTEA is PostgreSQL’s binary type; uploaded files live here.
- **Line 14:** Credit or author text, empty by default.
- **Line 15:** Link to the page that explains the source or licence.
- **Line 16:** Creation time with timezone, defaulting to the moment the row is inserted. Used to purge abandoned uploads.
- **Line 17:** Declares id as the primary key (unique identifier).
- **Line 18:** Foreign key to lessons(id). ON DELETE CASCADE deletes attachments when their lesson is deleted; ON UPDATE CASCADE would follow an id change.
- **Line 19:** Only image, video and youtube are allowed as kind.
- **Line 20:** Only upload, link and suggested are allowed as origin.
- **Line 21:** An upload must have data and no url; anything else must have a url and no data.
- **Line 22:** Closes the parenthesised expression or call and ends the statement.
- **Line 23:** Index on lesson_id so a lesson’s attachments are found quickly.
- **Line 24:** Commits the transaction, making the table permanent.

## client/api-proxy.js

Exact path: `C:\Users\barri\OneDrive\Desktop\Next Chapter Projects\CoachLab\client\api-proxy.js`

Streams local API requests to Express so larger media downloads do not stall in Vite.

### Lines 1–26

```text
1 | // Streams local API requests to Express so larger media downloads do not stall in Vite.
2 | import http from 'node:http';
3 |
4 | // Vite's built-in proxy stalls on downloads over about 1 MB, so /api is forwarded with plain piped streams instead.
5 | // Uses a streaming proxy so local API responses do not need to fit in one memory buffer.
6 | export function apiProxy(port) {
7 |   return {
8 |     name: 'coachlab-api-proxy',
9 |     // Installs the local API forwarding middleware when Vite starts.
10 |     configureServer(server) {
11 |       server.middlewares.use('/api', (request, response) => {
12 |         const upstream = http.request({ host: '127.0.0.1', port, method: request.method, path: request.originalUrl, headers: { ...request.headers, host: `127.0.0.1:${port}`, 'x-forwarded-for': request.socket.remoteAddress } }, answer => {
13 |           response.writeHead(answer.statusCode, answer.headers);
14 |           answer.pipe(response);
15 |         });
16 |         upstream.on('error', () => {
17 |           if (response.headersSent) return response.destroy();
18 |           response.writeHead(502, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
19 |           response.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'The CoachLab backend is not reachable.' }));
20 |         });
21 |         response.on('close', () => upstream.destroy());
22 |         request.pipe(upstream);
23 |       });
24 |     },
25 |   };
26 | }
```

- **Line 1:** Human-readable comment: Streams local API requests to Express so larger media downloads do not stall in Vite. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 2:** Imports Node’s http module for making a plain request to the backend on this computer.
- **Line 3:** Blank line separates related sections for readability; it performs no operation.
- **Line 4:** Human-readable comment: Vite's built-in proxy stalls on downloads over about 1 MB, so /api is forwarded with plain piped streams instead. Comments explain intent and are not executed.
- **Line 5:** Human-readable comment: Uses a streaming proxy so local API responses do not need to fit in one memory buffer. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 6:** Exports apiProxy, a function that takes the backend’s port and returns a Vite plugin object.
- **Line 7:** Returns an object containing the fixture's helper functions.
- **Line 8:** A name that appears in Vite’s messages.
- **Line 9:** Human-readable comment: Installs the local API forwarding middleware when Vite starts. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 10:** configureServer is called by Vite when the development server starts; it receives the server.
- **Line 11:** Registers a handler for every address starting with /api. request is what the browser sent, response is what will be returned.
- **Line 12:** The development proxy now also forwards the real address of the browser in an x-forwarded-for header (replacing any value the browser supplied). The backend uses it to rate-limit sign-in attempts per device instead of treating every request as coming from the proxy.
- **Line 13:** Copies the backend’s status code and headers to the browser’s response.
- **Line 14:** pipe sends the backend’s body to the browser piece by piece, waiting whenever the browser is busy, so large files stream correctly.
- **Line 15:** Ends the /api handler.
- **Line 16:** Handles the case where the backend cannot be reached.
- **Line 17:** If the answer already started, just closes the connection because the headers cannot be changed.
- **Line 18:** Otherwise sends status 502 (Bad Gateway) as JSON.
- **Line 19:** Sends a plain-language message; the page shows it as a connection problem.
- **Line 20:** Ends the /api handler.
- **Line 21:** If the browser disconnects, cancels the backend request so nothing keeps running.
- **Line 22:** Streams the browser’s request body (for example an uploaded file) to the backend.
- **Line 23:** Ends the /api handler.
- **Line 24:** Ends configureServer, followed by a comma because it is a property.
- **Line 25:** Ends the plugin object.
- **Line 26:** Ends the function.

## prisma/migrations/20261016150000_add_accounts_and_ownership/migration.sql

Exact path: `C:\Users\barri\OneDrive\Desktop\Next Chapter Projects\CoachLab\prisma\migrations\20261016150000_add_accounts_and_ownership\migration.sql`

PostgreSQL migration for accounts and ownership. It only ADDS things: five new auth tables, a nullable owner_id column on lessons and on lesson_media, and their indexes and foreign keys. It never changes or deletes an existing lesson or attachment, which is why lessons that existed before accounts simply have an empty owner. It runs in one transaction. It was verified in a disposable schema first, then applied to the Development database after a verified backup (the lesson fingerprint was identical before and after).

## server/migrations/003_add_ownership.sql

Exact path: `C:\Users\barri\OneDrive\Desktop\Next Chapter Projects\CoachLab\server\migrations\003_add_ownership.sql`

Third SQLite migration. It adds an owner column to lessons and attachments. Existing rows keep an empty owner, which means nobody can see them until they are deliberately claimed.

### Lines 1–4

```text
1 | ALTER TABLE lessons ADD COLUMN owner_id TEXT;
2 | ALTER TABLE lesson_media ADD COLUMN owner_id TEXT;
3 | CREATE INDEX lessons_owner_id_idx ON lessons (owner_id);
4 | CREATE INDEX lesson_media_owner_id_idx ON lesson_media (owner_id);
```

- **Line 1:** Adds owner_id (the id of the coach who owns the lesson) to lessons. TEXT matches Better Auth’s text user ids. Existing rows get NULL (no owner).
- **Line 2:** Adds owner_id to attachments, so an unsaved upload also belongs to someone.
- **Line 3:** Index so listing one coach’s lessons stays fast.
- **Line 4:** Index so listing one coach’s attachments stays fast.

## server/request-guard.js

Exact path: `C:\Users\barri\OneDrive\Desktop\Next Chapter Projects\CoachLab\server\request-guard.js`

Bounds production API traffic and rejects compressed bodies before they are parsed. Limits traffic and memory growth before request-body parsing.

### Lines 1–23

```text
1 | // Bounds production API traffic and rejects compressed bodies before they are parsed.
2 | // Limits traffic and memory growth before request-body parsing.
3 | export function productionApiGuard({ now = Date.now, limit = 120, maxClients = 1024 } = {}) {
4 |   const clients = new Map();
5 |   const windowMs = 60000;
6 |   return (request, response, next) => {
7 |     if (request.method === 'GET' && request.path === '/health') return next();
8 |     const time = now();
9 |     for (const [key, entry] of clients) if (entry.until <= time) clients.delete(key);
10 |     const key = request.ip || request.socket.remoteAddress;
11 |     let entry = clients.get(key);
12 |     if (!entry) {
13 |       if (clients.size >= maxClients) return response.set('Retry-After', '60').status(503).json({ error: 'The server is busy. Please try again shortly.' });
14 |       entry = { count: 0, until: time + windowMs };
15 |       clients.set(key, entry);
16 |     }
17 |     entry.count++;
18 |     if (entry.count > limit) return response.set('Retry-After', String(Math.max(1, Math.ceil((entry.until - time) / 1000)))).status(429).json({ error: 'Too many requests. Please wait a minute and try again.' });
19 |     const encoding = String(request.headers['content-encoding'] || 'identity').trim().toLowerCase();
20 |     if (encoding !== 'identity') return response.status(415).json({ error: 'Compressed request bodies are not supported. Send an uncompressed request.' });
21 |     next();
22 |   };
23 | }
```

- **Line 1:** Human-readable comment: Bounds production API traffic and rejects compressed bodies before they are parsed. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 2:** Human-readable comment: Limits traffic and memory growth before request-body parsing. This explanation does not execute.
- **Line 3:** Exports a middleware factory with a clock, request limit and maximum tracked addresses; defaults allow 120 API requests per minute and at most 1,024 entries. Tests can supply small deterministic values.
- **Line 4:** Creates an in-memory map from client address to count and expiration; each server process has its own map.
- **Line 5:** Sets the counting window to sixty thousand milliseconds, or one minute.
- **Line 6:** Returns the Express middleware function which receives the request, response and next-handler callback.
- **Line 7:** Exempts only GET health checks so hosting health probes remain available even when the limiter is full. The path is relative to the /api mount.
- **Line 8:** Reads the clock once so cleanup and response calculations use a consistent time.
- **Line 9:** Deletes expired address entries before counting; iteration is bounded by maxClients.
- **Line 10:** Uses the proxy-validated client IP, falling back to the socket address only if unavailable. No caller-supplied account ID controls this key.
- **Line 11:** Looks up this address’s current counting window.
- **Line 12:** Starts a fresh counter only when this address has no unexpired entry.
- **Line 13:** Rejects new addresses with 503 and a retry hint when the map is full; does not allocate unbounded memory or evict active counters to bypass limits.
- **Line 14:** Starts this address at zero requests with an expiry one minute from now.
- **Line 15:** Stores the new bounded counter in the map.

Allocates a predictable lesson schedule and repairs only small timing differences.

### Lines 1–21

```text
1 | // Allocates a predictable lesson schedule and repairs only small timing differences.
2 | import { sections, validateDraft } from '../client/src/lesson-draft.js';
3 |
4 | // Splits requested minutes across five sections so the provider gets explicit targets.
5 | export function sectionSchedule(duration) {
6 |   const minutes = [0.15, 0.25, 0.30, 0.20].map(share => Math.floor(duration * share));
7 |   minutes.push(duration - minutes.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0));
8 |   return sections.map((name, index) => ({ name, minutes: minutes[index] }));
9 | }
10 |
11 | // Repairs only a small timing mismatch; larger or malformed results must still fail validation.
12 | export function reconcileDraftTiming(draft, request) {
13 |   if (!Array.isArray(draft?.sections) || draft.sections.some(section => !Number.isInteger(section?.minutes))) return draft;
14 |   const total = draft.sections.reduce((sum, section) => sum + section.minutes, 0);
15 |   const difference = request.duration_minutes - total;
16 |   if (!difference || Math.abs(difference) > Math.min(2, request.duration_minutes * 0.05)) return draft;
17 |   if (validateDraft(draft, { ...request, duration_minutes: total })) return draft;
18 |   const longest = draft.sections.reduce((best, section, index, items) => section.minutes > items[best].minutes ? index : best, 0);
19 |   const corrected = { ...draft, sections: draft.sections.map((section, index) => index === longest ? { ...section, minutes: section.minutes + difference } : section) };
20 |   return validateDraft(corrected, request) ? draft : corrected;
21 | }
```

```text
1 | // Shares a small in-memory YouTube search allowance across both search routes; restarts reset it.
2 | export class YouTubeQuotaError extends Error {
3 |   // null
4 |   constructor() { super('YouTube search allowance reached. Try later; curated videos and manual links remain available.'); this.status = 429; }
5 | }
6 |
7 | // Shares rolling-day counters in this process only; a restart clears them.
8 | export function createYouTubeQuota(now = Date.now) {
9 |   let calls = [];
10 |   return {
11 |     // Reserves quota before an actual search, so simultaneous routes cannot overspend this process's allowance.
12 |     take(userId) {
13 |       const time = now();
14 |       calls = calls.filter(call => time - call.time < 86400000);
15 |       if (calls.length >= 80 || (userId && calls.filter(call => call.userId === userId).length >= 25)) throw new YouTubeQuotaError();
16 |       calls.push({ time, userId });
17 |     },
18 |   };
19 | }
20 |
21 | export const youtubeQuota = createYouTubeQuota();
```
